# Delta Pressure Delta Pressure is the difference in pressure between two areas. This difference can cause [bold]pressure damage[/bold] to fragile objects between them.
Windows, Windoors, Shutters, and Inflatable Walls can break from these pressure differences, allowing the gas to flow freely through them.
When these items break vary based on material, and practically speaking, seeing differences above [color=orange]1000kPa[/color] is incredible rare.
## Breaking points
If you're curious, below are the breaking points of all relevant objects. All directional windows can only withstand a quarter of the pressure a solid window can.
### Standard Glass and Objects
Standard full-size glass and other weak objects can withstand a Delta Pressure up to [color=orange][protodata="Window" comp="DeltaPressure" member="MinPressureDelta"/] kPa[/color] before starting to crack.
### Reinforced Glass
Reinforced full-size glass can withstand a Delta Pressure up to [color=orange][protodata="ReinforcedWindow" comp="DeltaPressure" member="MinPressureDelta"/] kPa[/color].
### Plasma Glass
Normal and Reinforced Plasma glass can withstand a Delta Pressure up to [color=orange][protodata="ReinforcedPlasmaWindow" comp="DeltaPressure" member="MinPressureDelta"/] kPa[/color].
